title: H2: bind the nominal marker packet to a written head without fitting separate verb valencies
phase: Exposed exploratory manual construction; no translation, new census, decoder or reserved test.

decision_note.unknown: Can H_post_U obtain one written outer governor with the same operation in both retained cheol daiin contexts, without fitting different predicate valencies?
decision_note.predecessor_check: IDEA819 only refuted its old fixed of-basin modifier;930 immediate nominal-head rule failed,1140 qotaiin scope was unresolved. None provides a reusable lexical value. Prior U marker semantics and H nominal cheol remain hypothetical.
decision_note.outcome_changes: A forced predicate interpretation would need per-whole valencies and retain missing-marker countercases; do not adopt it. A common nominal operation can resolve the written head but remains a noun phrase, not a full assertion. Neither outcome warrants a corpus parser or more guessed head classes.
decision_note.smallest_adequate_work: Author the same local operation at the two seed passages; retain entire IT f24r.1-19 and f102v1.13-14 paragraphs; inspect already known whole-form countercontexts and source differences; independent semantic/source review.
decision_note.wall_time_budget: 30 minutes total including retrieval, manual construction, source review and publication, starting approximately13:34UTC. No further implementation or control expansion within this block.

H2.inventory: Existing H supplies nominal cheol C(z). Only qotaiin and qokar are newly licensed as whole nominal head descriptions QT(w) and QK(w). No q-prefix meaning, inner segmentation or general head inventory is assumed.
H2.operation: An H nominal expression with referent z, followed by one contiguous U marker run, can attach to the immediately next exact licensed nominal head. Bind its pending e_outer to that written head occurrence referent w. Preserve every Role_s(w)=z in the packet and return the nominal expression headed by w.
H2.fixed_marker_content: Role_s(governor)=dependent remains single-valued for each s. Distinct roles may have the same dependent. No mandatory slot inventory is introduced; no missing OR slot is filled.
H2.boundary: No skipping; no uncertain seam or drawing bridge; own-reader paragraph scope required. Clear within-paragraph line wraps may be crossed as an explicit syntactic hypothesis. Consume the next head once. Further composition would require the same declared rule, not automatic classification of later unknown words.
H2.types_and_identity: w is the actual written nominal head referent, not an invented event. The result is nominal, not an assertion. No w=z or w!=z; different occurrences of either written form do not establish identical individuals.

claim_bearing_prior_limits: qotaiin79/79/83 and qokar150/149/141 exact occurrences are broadly dispersed and prose-only; their profiles do not supply nominal type, verb valency or concrete meaning.
IDEA819 failed its finite adjacent-head modifier under old fixed guessed types; qokain flanks were nonnominal only inside that model. It does not refute qokar as a new governor.

GDT1140 qotaiin decomposition and NOT/FUTURE scope remain unselected; no operator value inherited.

reader_sensitivity: The cheol daiin or / qotaiin string is present in all three source readings, but raw group IDs and the surrounding forms differ. IT/ZL own flags permit the paragraph-local check; RF lacks own paragraph flags, so its cross-line scope is not independently validated.
cheol daiin qokar is a stable same-line exact core in all three. RF preceding @152;aiin qkol is not IT/ZL daiin qkol.
Other-reader spellings such as odaiin or okai{ikh}@221;l are retained; no normalization or joining.
Readers remain alternative readings of one manuscript, not replications.
decision: Retain H2 as an explicit local nominal binding with one shared operation. Do not call it a full clause or select qotaiin/qokar meanings. Do not expand the head inventory merely to cover more groups.
next_decision: The content-bearing obligation is now precise: any proposed DAIIN/OR account must allow both relations of one written qotaiin head to target the same cheol referent. A further step requires an already evidenced content relation or written identity contrast that distinguishes this shared target from nested relations; another bare nominal attachment does not settle it. No unchanged missing-input audit or generic parser expansion is selected.
